findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἀκούσαντες αὐτὰ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθαρισθῶσιν ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ σὺ δὲ μετ᾽ αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Then, after hearing them and doing them, they may be cleansed from their evils[q], and you also with them.
findings.issue: Replacing the purpose connector ἵνα with a new sentence beginning “Then” loses the explicit purpose linking the instruction to speak with the community’s cleansing through hearing and doing. The English retains hearing, doing, cleansing, and Hermas’s inclusion, but presents their relationship to the preceding command as temporal progression rather than stated purpose. Note q correctly describes the source’s purpose, but does not restore it in the reader text.
findings.suggested_revision: Reconnect the clauses: “speak[o] them all[p] into the ears of the holy ones, so that, after hearing them and doing them, they may be cleansed from their evils[q], and you also with them.” This proposed replacement requires fresh review before acceptance.

summary: Both editions were independently checked against all eleven source paragraphs. The standard edition preserves the selected working readings, conditions, negations, attribution, and difficult assertions without a concrete fidelity defect identified. The simplified edition needs to restore the explicit purpose connection in VIII.11. Both editions disclose the obelized infinitive and bracketed editorial “all,” and their witness notes are compatible with the supplied attributed reports. This review does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript images, handwriting, hashes, or exhaustive collation.
